chapter: Mandeville, Bunk Johnson and society banquets
title: Bunk Johnson teaching the Fritz band in Mandeville
summary: George recalls Bunk instructing Isidore Fritz's band across the lake, with Tommy Ladner, and George's own playing around Covington and Hammond.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Okay, it's going again. You were talking about Isidore Fritz and different people.

Yeah, I heard because Bunk was supposed to be instructing that band, Isidore Fritz, the old man Fritz, and Loya Fritz, and little Caggley who plays trumpet. B's brother, Kleyber, was playing the drum all this way with Tommy Ladner.
They all came from across the lake today and lived over there.
And where did Tommy Ladner play then?
Tommy Ladner played a while with that Sam Fritz band. Bunk would come over weekends when he was available, you know.
And what instrument was he playing that? Who that? Tommy Ladner. He started on trumpet, you think?
Yeah, that's what he was playing that night. I don't know what he started on, but that's what he was playing.
So many guys change, I want to check.
What about Covington, what is it, Beda Springs? Did you ever get around there?
I played in Beda Springs, I played in Covington, I played in Unita, Tick Faw, Hammond. All through in that neighborhood.
